learn.title: What is an equation?
learn.body: An equation says two things are equal, like $x+3=7$. The letter $x$ stands for a number we do not know yet. Solving the equation means finding that number.

learn.title: Keep it balanced
learn.body: Picture a balance scale. If you add or remove the same amount on both sides, it stays level. That is the one rule of equations: do the same thing to both sides.

learn.title: Solve $x+3=7$
learn.body: We want $x$ alone. Right now 3 is added to it, so we undo that.

learn.title: Solve $2x=10$
learn.body: Here $x$ is multiplied by 2, so we undo that by dividing.

learn.title: Fractions with the same bottom
learn.body: When the denominators match, you only add the numerators: $\frac{a}{b}+\frac{c}{b}=\frac{a+c}{b}$. For example $\frac{2}{7}+\frac{3}{7}=\frac{5}{7}$.

learn.title: Reading notation
learn.body: $x^2$ means $x$ times itself and is called a square. $\sqrt{x}$ is the root, the number that squares to $x$. $|x|$ is the absolute value, the distance from zero.
Do the opposite: adding undoes subtracting, and multiplying undoes dividing. Then check by putting your answer back into the equation.

questions.explanation: Same denominator, so add the numerators.

questions.prompt: Match each notation with its name.
questions.explanation: A square multiplies by itself, a root undoes it, and the bars give distance from zero.

questions.prompt: Solve $2x+3=7$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Undo the operations in reverse order: first the addition, then the multiplication.

questions.prompt: Which point on the line is $x=3$?
questions.explanation: Point B sits three steps right of zero.
